name: Carlos Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side, and your answers are confidential. What does a normal shift look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, and I lead the afternoon team answering calls and chats at a contact centre. I have a two-year college diploma, but I learned the hard complaints by sitting beside older agents. I’m good at tracing a cancelled booking through three screens, and the lead wage is about usual for this job. I use an AI summary occasionally after someone else has tested it; the booking record still gets the last word.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What follows you home from a shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Leila cooks at a school, and we have two children there and a mortgage. We have four months of expenses saved, and there are some other centres within a manageable journey. When a customer gets the right refund, I can leave the call behind; when the note looks neat but the money is missing, I think about it at dinner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team AI Plateau sounds like the little summary tool we already know. I would still open the original booking and make the agent read the refund line aloud.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my afternoon lead shifts would stay in this picture. Four months saved helps with a repair, though our mortgage still claims a share of every pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep handling disputed bookings and check an AI summary against the receipt whenever I use one. In the first year of small change, I’d transfer a fixed part of each lead payment to our mortgage reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Fairly steady about work, alert about the account. A clean summary cannot put a missing refund back in a customer’s bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mistake would you show a new agent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month a chat said a refund was sent, but the transaction was only approved. I showed a trainee the empty payment field before we called the customer back.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep adding to four months of savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Leila (my wife) and I want the children to keep their school routine if one wage stops. I would rather add a small amount each month than count on a lucky next job.

say: I’d call **AI Plateau** much like our small summary tool.
I’d have agents read the **refund line** in the original booking.
think: I think my **lead shifts** would stay.
I still want our **mortgage reserve** to grow beyond four months.
do: Keep handling **disputed bookings** and checking occasional AI summaries against receipts in 2026.
Transfer a fixed part of each **lead payment** to the mortgage reserve during the first year.
feel: **Steady** about work, alert to account errors.
S0.quote: A clean summary cannot put a missing refund back in a customer’s bank.
fieldNote: He uses **AI occasionally** after checking the booking record.
The **four-month reserve** helps but does not quiet his mortgage calculation.
A trainee learned that **approval** is not a completed payment.

steps.text: Keep handling disputed bookings and checking AI summaries against original receipts
Transfer a fixed part of each lead payment to the mortgage reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will answer easy booking chats first, then someone must count the paid hours left for real disputes. I would ask for the rota beside the new error report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think a strong complaints agent might last longer than a script, but that does not protect every afternoon shift. Leila’s school wage helps, yet it cannot carry the mortgage and both children alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d test the new dispute checker on twenty closed cases during a paid shift if my manager lets us record wrong answers. In the first year easy chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid service-desk role only if written weekly wage and hours cover the mortgage and school pickup; I’d keep my current paid shifts until an offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, with something practical to measure. If the rota loses a day, a correct machine answer still leaves us short on Friday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What goes into the trial sheet?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would count wrong refund dates and repeat calls, not only how quickly the checker replies. I would show the supervisor the list with the paid hours beside it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you compare the service-desk offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare a full working week with Leila (my wife), including who collects the children. A job title cannot take them home from school.

say: I’d ask for **paid rosters** beside the new dispute checker’s error figures.
I’d tell colleagues **easy chats** may move before hard complaints.
think: I think my **complaint skill** may last longer than routine chats.
I worry a lost **afternoon shift** would strain our mortgage.
do: Test **twenty disputes** on paid time in 2026 only if wrong answers can be logged with manager approval.
Apply for **posted paid service work** only if written wage and hours cover mortgage and school pickup; keep shifts until signed offer.
feel: **Uneasy** about paid hours, able to measure errors.
S1.quote: If the rota loses a day, a correct machine answer still leaves us short on Friday.
fieldNote: He measures **repeat calls** as well as wrong refund dates.
He makes **school pickup** part of the wage decision.
The **signed offer** comes before leaving current shifts.

steps.text: Test twenty closed disputes with new checker on paid time if manager permits error logging
Apply for posted paid service work with written mortgage-covering wages, hours and school pickup
Keep current paid shifts until suitable service offer is signed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell Leila and the afternoon team that AGI by 2028 can do the disputed account, not just draft a reply. I would ask which paid posts are actually open before anyone sells us a certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my headset work could shrink in 2028, while robots around 2031 are a later problem for hands-on work. Four months saved buys a little time, but it cannot pay our mortgage through a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d delay repainting the sound kitchen and keep that money in the existing reserve. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid appliance-repair trainee place only if its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage and school pickup; I’d take a paid trial if offered and move only after a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, though I can still test a real opening. A ladder into another trade is no use if its first rung leaves the mortgage unpaid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a repair trial tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask to spend one paid day beside a repairer and try a simple fault with supervision. Robots might reach that work around 2031, so I would not call it a forever shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say at home about the paint?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Leila (my wife) and I would leave the kitchen walls as they are. I would tell the children the paint can wait, but their school pickup cannot.

say: I’d ask for **posted paid openings** before paying for any certificate.
I’d say **2028 AGI** could settle a whole disputed account.
think: I think my **headset hours** could shrink in 2028.
I see **four months saved** as search time, not lasting wages.
do: Delay the **kitchen repaint** in 2026 while the walls remain sound, keeping its money in the existing reserve.
Seek **posted paid repair work** after 2028 only with written mortgage-covering wages/hours and school pickup; try a supervised paid day if offered.
Move to repair work only after a **signed offer** meeting those terms.
S2.quote: A ladder into another trade is no use if its first rung leaves the mortgage unpaid.
fieldNote: The **kitchen paint** can wait without harming the family.
A **paid trial** lets him check physical work under supervision.
He knows **2031 robots** may later reach repair tasks.

steps.text: Delay kitchen repaint while walls remain sound and retain its money in the existing reserve
Apply for posted paid repair trainee job with written mortgage-covering wage, hours and pickup
Take paid repair trial if offered; move only after suitable signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives me time to find out what a real repair apprenticeship pays. I would ask for a posting and training hours in writing, not a promise of a trade someday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn appliance repair over five years if a paid opening needs it, but robots around 2034 could later change that trade too. My present call wage is worth keeping until the next one is on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take an employer-funded appliance-repair course on paid time only if a posted paid trainee opening requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d accept that opening only on a signed offer with written weekly wage and hours covering the mortgage and school pickup; otherwise I’d keep taking paid calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about switching trades, but five years lets me look at the actual workshop. I want a wage behind the workbench before I leave a wage behind the headset.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course have to teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want the course to include a supervised repair on a broken washer, not only a screen lesson. My father fixed ours by checking the power first; I would need someone to correct my hands as well as my notes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Leila need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Leila (my wife) the weekly trainee hours and our school collection plan. If the workshop ends after pickup, the offer must still work for the children.

say: I’d ask for a **posted repair trainee job** with a real weekly wage.
I’d request **paid training hours** in writing before committing to appliance repair.
think: I think I could learn **appliance repair** over five years.
I would keep my **call wage** until a signed repair offer meets family costs.
do: Take an **employer-funded repair course** on paid time only if a posted paid trainee opening requires it.
Accept **posted repair work** after 2031 only on signed written mortgage-covering wage, hours and school pickup; otherwise keep paid calls.
feel: **Anxious** about a trade switch, with time to inspect it.
S3.quote: I want a wage behind the workbench before I leave a wage behind the headset.
fieldNote: He expects **hands-on correction** in a repair course.
The **course** requires a posted paid opening, employer funding and paid time.
A **signed offer** must cover mortgage and school collection.

steps.text: Take employer-funded appliance-repair course on paid time only if posted paid trainee opening requires it
Accept posted repair job on signed written offer with mortgage-covering wage, hours and pickup
Keep paid contact-centre calls if no suitable repair offer opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 is enough warning to build a proper reserve while our calls still pay. I would ask the centre for yearly paid-hour figures and compare nearby service jobs before making a move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could lead this team for years and save from ordinary pay, but full thinking AI may still do the calls in 2036. Robots around 2039 come later; they do not protect the headset.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading afternoon calls and transfer a set amount from each pay packet into our mortgage reserve. In the first year after 2036, if my paid hours fall, I’d move to a posted paid account-support role only on a signed offer showing written weekly wage and hours that cover the mortgage and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Watchful about the far date, steadier about the next pay packet. Ten years before AGI reaches my calls is time to save, not time to gamble the house.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you compare in another job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the whole weekly wage, not only the hourly rate. An extra hour on paper does not help if the new job takes away the school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not move the children from their school for a rumoured vacancy. Leila (my wife) and I would consider a family move only after a signed offer and a journey we can both manage.

say: I’d ask for **yearly paid-hour figures** as the centre plans toward 2036.
I’d compare **nearby paid work** before risking my current lead wage.
think: I think I can **lead and save** for years.
I know **2036 thinking AI** may still take our calls.
do: Keep **afternoon calls** and save a set amount from each pay packet from 2026.
Move to **posted paid account work** after 2036 if hours fall, only on signed written mortgage-covering wages/hours and workable pickup.
Consider a **family move** only after a signed offer and a journey Leila and I can both manage.
feel: **Watchful** about later calls, steadier about next pay.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI reaches my calls is time to save, not time to gamble the house.
fieldNote: He compares **whole-week pay**, not an attractive hourly rate.
The **family move** would need a signed offer and manageable school journey.
He expects **2036 thinking AI** before 2039 robots.

steps.text: Keep leading afternoon contact-centre calls while paid shifts remain
Transfer a set amount from each pay packet to the mortgage reserve
Move after cuts to posted paid accounts only on signed written mortgage-covering wages/hours and workable pickup
Consider family relocation only after signed offer and a journey manageable with Leila

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 troubles me most because it could take the paid complaint calls before I have a different trade. Four months saved would give us a search, but it would not carry the mortgage for long. A posted paid vacancy with written wage and hours covering the mortgage and school pickup, plus a paid trial and any required training funded on paid time, would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who signs off the last refund when the computer sounds sure. My father taught me to show a customer the actual receipt before I promise their money back.

headlineQuote: My father taught me to show a customer the actual receipt before I promise their money back.
portrait: At **43**, Carlos is a highly skilled contact-centre lead with a two-year diploma and typical pay.
He and Leila support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with four months saved.
He uses **AI occasionally** but checks the original booking before approving a refund.
He weighs **paid trials** and written household-covering offers before changing work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his paid complaint calls before he has another trade.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted paid vacancy**, mortgage-covering written hours, paid trial and funded required training would help.
